records.name: Calm Clarity
records.summary: Teaches leadership and communication skills based on brain science, so people and teams can think clearly under pressure. Workshops are online, and the group also offers a free brain pattern assessment.
records.what_you_do: Register for a virtual workshop or the 6-session cohort, take the free assessment, or sign up to volunteer.

schedule.text: Intro workshops are virtual, 90 minutes long, and held on several dates a year. The Foundation Program is a six week virtual cohort with two hour sessions on Wednesdays.

cost.text: No prices are listed for the workshops, the cohort, or the training. The brain pattern self-assessment is free, and so is a short summary guide that you get by filling out a form.

first_step.how: Register for an intro workshop from the events page, or email info@calmclarity.org with questions.
first_step.basis: Intro workshops have open public registration and the site lays out the steps to start, but the site is written for organizations and does not say beginners are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: The 90 minute virtual intro workshop introduces the group's brain pattern framework. The site aims its training at leaders, managers, and HR or learning staff, so expect a room of working professionals. The site lists no price for the workshop.
first_visit_tips: Listings show Eastern Time, so work out the start time in your own zone before you register.
Take the free brain pattern self-assessment first if you want a taste of the material.

records.notes: The events calendar lists 15 virtual dates from Nov 2026 to Dec 2027, all in the future, so no past dated activity is recorded and status stays probably_active. Tier 1 named Nov 19, 2026 as the next date, but that was a half day Science of Listening session for coaches and leaders, not the intro workshop, so it is removed from the schedule. The Dec 10, 2026 intro listing prints 12 pm ET, but its web address suggests 7 pm, so confirm the start time at registration. The site says it sells its training mainly to organizations; the open enrollment is the intro workshop and one yearly cohort. The site says it is c/o CultureTrust Greater Philadelphia; see the top level notes.

records.name: Calvary Athletic Association
records.summary: A Northeast Philadelphia youth sports association with in-house and travel teams in baseball, softball, basketball, football, cheer, volleyball, and lacrosse. Young kids can start in in-house programs at age 3.
records.what_you_do: Kids play on in-house or travel teams. Families can also volunteer for board seats or the parents' clubs; the board positions are voluntary.

schedule.text: Teams play in seasons, spring and fall, with games at sites across the city. The club does not publish practice days or times.

cost.text: In-house programs are $90 or $110. Travel teams are $165 or $185. Tackle football and competition cheer are $210 or $230. A girls AAU volleyball listing shows an $800 flat fee. Online registration adds a $5 to $7 fee. The fee page does not say which year it covers.

first_step.how: Choose your child's program on the club's Registration page and fill out the form. A confirmation email follows. In-house programs start at age 3.
first_step.basis: Registration is open online and in-house programs take young children, but the site does not give practice times, tryout rules, or a welcome page for new families.
first_step.what_to_expect: Kids play in-house or on travel teams at home sites and other fields across the city. Practice days and times are not published, so ask the club when the first practice is. Fees vary by program, and the fee page does not say which year it covers.
first_visit_tips: Read the Code of Conduct before you register: it sets sportsmanship rules for parents at games.
Ask the club when practices start, since the site does not post them.
Ask how travel team tryouts or evaluations work, because the site does not explain them.
Check which year the fee page covers with the club before you pay.

records.notes: The homepage shows board nominations on Oct 12 and a clothing pre-order closing Oct 8, but neither prints a year, so neither is used. Tier 1 online_ok true reflected online registration, not online play, so the field is removed. Volleyball, lacrosse, and cheer have no exact interest tag, so the nearest sports tags are used for the club as a whole. The Mother's Club page has no description. The contact email sits behind email protection, so none is recorded.

records.name: Camphor Memorial United Methodist Church
records.summary: A United Methodist church that runs a food cupboard, a community ministry, a van ministry, and children's and youth programs.
records.what_you_do: Call the church to ask about the food cupboard, Sunday school, or the Youth Fellowship for ages 12 to 18. The church website also lists its ministries.

schedule.text: The church site does not publish worship times, food cupboard days, Sunday school times, or Youth Fellowship meeting times. Call 215-747-2600 to ask.

cost.text: The site does not list costs for its programs.

first_step.how: Call the church office at 215-747-2600 and ask about the food cupboard, Sunday school, or the Youth Fellowship.
first_step.basis: The church is open to the public and gives a phone number, but its site has no welcome page for visitors and no worship, food, or class times.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Youth Fellowship is for ages 12 to 18. Its meetings mix talk about faith and relationships with food, games, and service projects, and the group has gone on outings such as bowling and retreats. The site does not give meeting days or times, or say whether visitors may come before joining.
first_visit_tips: Call ahead, since the site lists no meeting days or times.
Ask the food cupboard about its distribution days and whether it needs ID before you go.

records.notes: Food cupboard hours, distribution rules, and worship times are not on any page I could read. A web search surfaced a third party pantry listing with a Tuesday morning window, but the search summary said listings conflict and I could not open that listing, so no hours are recorded. The church footer email is garbled, so none is recorded. The home page mentions a $100,000 National Fund for Sacred Places grant with no clear date, so it is not used. The group pages on the church site ask visitors to join or log in; I did not do that.

records.name: Cathedral Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul
records.summary: The mother church of the Catholic Archdiocese of Philadelphia, open to anyone who wants to pray or attend Mass. Its website lists weekend and weekday Mass times and a public phone line.
records.what_you_do: Attend Mass in the Basilica or the Cathedral Chapel, including a Spanish Mass on Sunday. The site also lists nine volunteer ministries, from greeters and lectors to music and visits to the sick.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 8, 9:30 and 11 am (the 11 am Mass is livestreamed), a Spanish Mass at 12:30 pm in the Cathedral Chapel, and a 6:30 pm Mass. Weekday Masses at 7:15 am and 12:05 pm, a Saturday Mass at 12:05 pm, and an anticipated Saturday Mass at 5:15 pm.

locations.label: Cathedral Basilica (at 18th Street and the Benjamin Franklin Parkway)

cost.text: The site lists no fee to attend Mass, and it does not ask for a donation at Mass.

access.notes: Three outside doors have ramps. Only the door off the main parking lot has an automatic push button, and the other doors need someone to open them. The site describes the building as limited for wheelchair access.

first_step.how: Come to any Mass on the schedule. To ask about joining or registering, call the parish office at (215) 561-1313 or talk with a priest after Mass.
first_step.basis: The site has a Welcoming Committee that calls newly registered families, a clear way to register, and Mass open to anyone. It describes no separate class for visitors.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is held in the Basilica or the Cathedral Chapel at set times, and a Spanish Mass is offered on Sunday. The site does not say how long Mass runs or where to sit, but greeters are there to welcome and seat people. You do not need to sign up to attend.
first_visit_tips: On Saturdays, Sundays, and Holy Days, visitors can park in the parish lot at 222 North 17th Street.
Use the door off the main parking lot, which has the automatic push button.
The 11 am Sunday Mass is livestreamed if you cannot come in person.
Call the parish office at (215) 561-1313 with questions before you come.

records.notes: All nine ministries are contacted through the parish office, and no training or background check is named for any role, so none is recorded. The site never states in so many words that Mass is free; the free level rests on no fee being listed, as in tier 1. Confession times conflict for the Spanish slot (12 pm by appointment in one place, 11:45 am to 12:15 pm in another), so none are recorded. Cathedral Shop, inside the Basilica: 215-665-9032, Sunday 10:30 am to 6:30 pm, Wednesday 10:30 am to 2 pm, Saturday 11 am to 5:15 pm. Groups can tour when the Basilica is open with no reservation, and the site asks them to email ahead.

records.name: Philadelphia Episcopal Cathedral
records.summary: The cathedral of the Episcopal Diocese of Pennsylvania in Center City. It holds a Sunday 10 am service and noonday services on Wednesdays and Fridays, and it has a newcomers form and a survey to help people find a ministry.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday Eucharist at 10 am or a noon Eucharist on a Wednesday or Friday, fill out the newcomers form, or take the survey to find a ministry. Volunteers can also help with the food pantry and other Cathedral Table Ministries.

schedule.text: Sunday Holy Eucharist at 10 am. Noonday Eucharist on Wednesdays and Fridays (the page does not give the time). The Cathedral Table Ministries food pantry runs Mondays from 9:30 to 11 am, and a community dinner is listed for Wednesdays at 6 pm with a partner group.

cost.text: Services and Evensong are free. Members are encouraged to give, with no amount set.

access.notes: The site names the Blue Line to 40th Street, then a walk east to 38th Street, and the Green Line streetcar to 36th Street.

first_step.how: Attend the 10 am Sunday Holy Eucharist, or fill out the newcomers form linked on the site.
first_step.basis: The site invites newcomers to fill out a newcomers form, has a ministry survey to help people find a place to serve, and says everyone is welcome at coffee hour.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Sunday service is a Holy Eucharist at 10 am that follows an ancient order of worship. The music for each Sunday is listed on the site, and a service leaflet is available as a download. The site does not give the length of the service, and coffee hour and adult formation follow.
first_visit_tips: Download the service leaflet from the site before you come.
On Sundays, street parking near the Cathedral needs a permit from the ushers or the printable link on the site. The LAZ lot at 39th and Market is not available for worship.
If you take transit, ride the Blue Line to 40th Street and walk to 38th Street.
Stay for coffee hour after the 10 am service.

records.notes: The contact name The Organization in tier 1 came from IRS and nonprofit data and is a placeholder, so it is removed. The Early Learning Center on the campus is a child care business, so it is not recorded. The community page lists a food pantry, a dinner, and a clothing partner; the partner checks are in the top level notes.

records.name: Courtesy Stable
records.summary: A horse stable in Fairmount Park run by a nonprofit that cares for horses and protects the Wissahickon Valley. People can take riding lessons, ride the trails, and join monthly volunteer days.
records.what_you_do: Take private or semi-private riding lessons in the lighted outdoor ring, or ride the trails. Come to a monthly Volunteer Day to help beautify the parks and the stable. Boarding is also offered.

schedule.text: Lessons run year round and are booked as slots open. Monthly Volunteer Days help the parks and the barn, but the site does not give their day or time.

cost.text: Lesson prices are not printed. The site says to contact the stable for current pricing. Barn Days group events cost $50 per person, and lesson payment is due the day of the lesson unless paid in advance by cash or check.

requirements.gear: Hard-soled shoes with a heel, and a riding helmet whenever you are mounted. The stable provides a helmet if you do not have one.

first_step.how: Email barnmanager@courtesystable.org to ask for a first lesson, or call 215.482.8108. The stable keeps your email until a slot opens and then contacts you.
first_step.basis: The site says all levels are welcome, the first lesson includes an evaluation, and there is a clear email route. Lessons are booked as slots open, so the wait time is not stated.
first_step.what_to_expect: The first lesson includes an evaluation and covers grooming, tacking, mounting, and walking. Private and semi-private lessons run one hour with one instructor, and students must be at least 8 years old. Riders under 15 need a parent or guardian on the premises, and adults stay for the whole lesson.
first_visit_tips: Fill out the Rider Release Form, a PDF on the site, and bring it with you. Riding requires it.
Wear hard-soled shoes with a heel, and bring your own helmet with a harness and chin strap if you have one.
Leave pets at home, and do not smoke in or around the barn.
Ask about the price before you book, because lesson rates are not printed.

records.notes: Monthly Volunteer Day day, time, and sign-up are not on the pages read: the events page links to a calendar that could not be read. Lesson prices are not printed. Full and share boarding have no printed prices or availability. Trail rules for guests are not printed. The footer says copyright 2024 and the rider form file name has 2026; neither is used as evidence. Tier 1 email (cynbarn0421) is kept, and the riding page gives barnmanager@courtesystable.org for lesson bookings. Sandy Hill Farm, named as the referral for children under 8, is in leads_only.

records.name: CBS Community Center (Congregation Beth Solomon)
records.summary: A Jewish community center on Tomlinson Road in Northeast Philadelphia with davening services, a kollel, a mikvah, and programs for men, women, and youth.
records.what_you_do: Join davening services, men's learning or women's programming, youth programs, or the Pesach food drive. Sign up for weekly updates on the site.

schedule.text: Daily davening (prayer) services, with times posted on the synagogue's online portal rather than on the center's pages. Youth, women's, and men's programs meet on schedules the site does not print. The Pesach food drive runs once a year.

cost.text: No program fees are printed on the pages read. Donations are invited, and the site does not describe membership or dues.

first_step.how: Email info@cbscommunitycenter.com or call 215.671.1981 and ask how to join a program. Sign up for weekly updates with the form on the homepage.
first_step.basis: Programs are listed, and some have contacts, but the site does not say whether visitors can attend a service or class or how a newcomer starts.
first_visit_tips: Check the synagogue's online portal for davening times, since the center's pages do not print them.
For High Holiday services, reserve a seat with the online form or the paper form on the site.
Call the office before you come to ask whether visitors can join.

records.notes: The newest dated item is a 2026 High Holiday seating reservation form with no month printed, so status is set to active while last_sign_of_life is left blank. Footer copyright 2024 and 2024 image dates are not used. Davening times, High Holiday dates, and program start dates are not printed on the pages read. RAJE Philly (men and women ages 18 to 30, Sunday afternoon program, contact on the programming page) and the Momentum Women's Trip are listed without dates, so they are not in the schedule. Somerton Kollel and Philadelphia Hatzolah were checked and not recorded; see the top level notes.

leads_only.name: Episcopal Community Services
leads_only.note: Named as a partner in the outreach list on the Philadelphia Episcopal Cathedral site. No link was printed on the page I read, and I did not find its website within the search budget. Not checked.

leads_only.name: Sandy Hill Farm
leads_only.note: Named on the Courtesy Stable riding page as the referral for children under 8. No link was printed. Not checked.

notes: Budget: 1 WebSearch used of 1. 36 WebFetch calls in total, 4 to 6 per group. No page was blocked, and none returned a 403 or a bot check. One accidental call to a Docs tool (an mcp__ read) was refused with a deny error and returned no data; I did not use any other non-permitted tool. Copyright footers, file names, and undated items were not used as evidence. Camphor food cupboard hours: a web search surfaced a third party pantry listing with a Tuesday morning window, but the search summary said listings conflict and I could not open that listing, so no hours are recorded. Leads checked and not recorded: (1) CultureWorks Greater Philadelphia, which the Calm Clarity site names as c/o CultureTrust Greater Philadelphia. It is a fiscal sponsor for about 120 projects, not a group to join. (2) Somerton Kollel (somertonkollel.org, linked from CBS). It is a Torah learning program at 11001 Philmont Pl with printed phone numbers, but the site does not say whether visitors can attend and gives no class times. Future research. (3) Philadelphia Hatzolah (philadelphiahatzolah.org). It is a volunteer emergency response group with a printed 24/7 line, but no volunteer steps or training are on the page. Future research. (4) University City Hospitality Coalition (uchcphiladelphia.org). The cathedral page names it as the provider of the Wednesday dinner. It has a volunteer email, but the sign-up steps and meal schedule were not on the pages I read. Future research. (5) Our Closet in Your Neighborhood (JFCS). It is a free pop-up program with a printed volunteer manager contact, but the page gives no public pop-up schedule. Future research. (6) Philabundance. It is named as a partner of the cathedral food pantry. It is a large regional food bank with its own volunteer system, so it is not recorded here. (7) The Early Learning Center on the cathedral campus is a child care business, so it is not recorded.
